problem: Portal V2 had strong functional coverage but visual scale, media sizing, chart containment and interaction consistency were still governed by multiple page-specific styles, allowing oversized components and inconsistent responsive behavior.
rootCause: Responsive behavior existed mainly as local CSS/test fixes rather than one cross-cutting experience contract that every present and dynamically rendered Portal V2 surface inherits.
preventionRule: Portal V2 must load one final experience contract that bounds content/media/chart scale, enforces 44px controls, visible keyboard focus, reduced-motion support, viewport-safe dialogs and no horizontal page overflow while preserving the canonical Portal State backend authority.
root_cause: Responsive behavior existed mainly as local CSS/test fixes rather than one cross-cutting experience contract that every present and dynamically rendered Portal V2 surface inherits.
prevention: Use portal-v2/experience.css and portal-v2/experience.js as the single final experience authority; do not introduce a parallel page-local UX layer.
Normalize and remeasure dynamically mounted visuals through MutationObserver and ResizeObserver.
Fail browser assurance on horizontal page overflow, marked visual overflow, missing experience runtime or critical controls below 44px.
Run the visual assurance matrix on six critical routes across 1440px, 1024px, 390px and 320px viewports.
Keep canonical Portal State authentication and stored=false backend failure behavior unchanged and fail-closed.
